learner_facing_text: Video Course 1 may teach assigned case/cabinet/cable logistics and product-recognition support while preserving processor configuration, calibration, receiving-card work, troubleshooting, rigging, structural and production-power authority with the responsible specialist/department.
notes: Physical support is product/system specific; no generic LED-wall assembly authorization is created.

learner_facing_text: Rental/touring LED panel families vary materially in physical hardware, connection/locking concepts, geometry and operating limits; familiarity with one product does not establish competence on another product family.
notes: Current ROE/Absen product evidence supports variability, not a universal handling procedure.

learner_facing_text: Any hands-on cabinet locking, alignment, magnetic-assist or physical panel-handling practice must be tied to the exact product/manual and qualified lead instruction; Course 1 should not present one generic physical technique as safe for all LED systems.
notes: Current 'repeat a locking step once shown' and magnet-snap technique require exact model/practitioner review before stronger release.

learner_facing_text: A dark, damaged or abnormal panel is reported through the video/LED work process; Course 1 does not authorize processor configuration, calibration, receiving-card service or independent troubleshooting/repair.

Staging Course 1 may teach assigned movement/staging, system recognition, component inventory and bounded support under a qualified lead without granting structural design, load-capacity, leveling, hardware-substitution, modification or final-acceptance authority.
notes: Specific modular-stage assembly belongs to exact manufacturer/product and qualified workplace instruction.

learner_facing_text: Modular staging systems can use materially different components, connections and manufacturer requirements; experience with one system does not authorize applying the same assembly/configuration method to another.
notes: Current course names Bil-Jax examples but exact manufacturer/manual evidence is still required for any retained physical practical.

learner_facing_text: Apparent completion or stability does not create authority to approve a stage/platform configuration, determine load capacity, substitute structural hardware or accept missing/changed safety components; those decisions remain with the responsible qualified/system authority.
notes: Recognition/reporting only; no structural acceptance criteria taught.

learner_facing_text: Scenic pieces are production assets with assignment-specific handling points and finished surfaces; the general learner should ask how/where a piece may be moved rather than inferring safe grip, drag, modification or repair from appearance.
notes: Requires practitioner/sector validation; no generic scenic movement technique is established.

learner_facing_text: Backline, Props and Wardrobe are separate crafts, but a shared early support layer can include assigned movement/staging of closed cases, racks, trunks, furniture or general production support while preserving department control over contents, presets, configuration and performer-specific items.
notes: Deeper technician/specialist pathways should split by department; exact support varies by production.

learner_facing_text: An assignment to move or stage an item does not automatically authorize changing its settings, contents, preset, packing method or condition; uncertain/show-critical/performer-specific items remain under the responsible department's direction.
notes: Useful work-control model; object-by-object permission is production specific.

learner_facing_text: Crew Blueprint's general-item → department-gear → show-critical-preset → performer-owned scale is an instructional prompt to increase verification as ownership/sensitivity rises; it is not a universal permission hierarchy and does not make any category automatically movable.
notes: Current Level 1 phrase 'freely movable' is too absolute and should be revised later; even general items can be positioned or restricted for safety/show/venue reasons.

learner_facing_text: Hazardous, regulated or specialist-controlled prop/effect items are excluded from ordinary general-stagehand handling and remain with the responsible qualified/authorized department or specialist process.
notes: Awareness boundary only; no operational hazardous-effect content belongs in this general support course.
